subject: Post-call recap: AcmeHealth private/VPC discovery & next steps
messages:
From: Camila Reyes <camila.reyes@redwood.ai>
To: Lisa Chen <lisa.chen@acmehealth.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 18 Nov 2026 15:02:00 -0800
Subject: Post-call recap: AcmeHealth private/VPC discovery & next steps

Hi Lisa — thanks again for the conversation today. Quick recap from our call and the next steps we discussed so everything is aligned.

Key drivers / pain points you shared:
- Regulatory & data residency: all PHI must remain in your AWS VPC and stored in the US region; SOC2 evidence and audit logs are baseline requirements.
- Network constraints: strict egress rules — customer-managed NAT and no outbound internet from the ML subnet; any external connections must go through a controlled proxy.
- Air-gap possibility: in certain regulated workflows you may need an air-gapped on-prem install for the inference runtime (no internet ingress/egress).
- KMS/HSM: keys must be customer-managed (AWS KMS or HSM) and key rotations need to be auditable.
- Timeline: target POC kickoff in ~6–8 weeks, production decision in 3–4 months.

Who we heard as stakeholders:
- Lisa Chen (Clinical AI) — product/clinical requirements
- Security (cc'd) — technical security & network constraints
- Procurement (procurement@acmehealth.com) — contracting and purchase order

Recap of Redwood fit & what we propose:
- Private/VPC deployment: Redwood Private with a customer-managed VPC connector. Our control plane can run via private peering; the inference runtime is deployed into the customer VPC (private subnets) and can be configured for zero outbound internet.
- Air-gapped on-prem option: we have an on-prem package that can be fully air-gapped; it requires minimal infra (2–4 GPU nodes for the POC depending on QPS) and our install runbook + Ansible playbook (link below).
- Security/compliance: we will provide SOC2 artifacts, architecture diagrams, audit log exports, and KMS integration docs.

Actions / next steps we agreed:
1) Technical deep-dive (security & networking) — Marissa (cc'd) to lead and propose times next week.
2) Share network diagram + SOC2 summary (attached) and a short checklist for firewall/proxy requirements.
3) Procurement: share a ballpark POC pricing and a draft mutual action plan — I’ll attach a pricing worksheet.
4) Security questionnaire: your security team to send any formal questionnaires or an initial list of evidence requests.

Attachments:
- network-diagram.png (high-level VPC connectivity)
- SOC2-summary.pdf (summary of controls and available artifacts)

Proposed dates: Marissa will propose 2x 60-minute slots for the technical deep-dive next Wed/Thu (Nov 25/26). If those don't work, please suggest alternatives.

Thanks again — happy to jump on a short screen share if helpful.

Best,
Camila Reyes

Date: Thu, 19 Nov 2026 09:37:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Post-call recap: AcmeHealth private/VPC discovery & next steps

Thanks Camila — really helpful summary and yes, that matches what we discussed. A couple quick clarifications: 

- Air-gap: when we say "air-gapped" we mean no external outbound traffic from the inference nodes. Is the on-prem package fully self-contained (no telemetry back to Redwood) or is there a lightweight control-plane agent that needs egress?
- POC sizing: happy to share expected QPS for typical clinical workload — roughly 15 concurrent requests at peak with 6–8k tokens/session. Will that fit in a 2–4 GPU POC?
- Security artifacts: I’ll have our security team send over a brief list (2–3 core items) by EOD Friday.

Can we schedule the technical deep-dive the week of Nov 23? Wed/Thu both look possible for Lisa & security. I’ll loop procurement after the technical call.

Best,
Lisa Chen
Clinical AI Lead, AcmeHealth
lisa.chen@acmehealth.com
